impact: A pooled object may be used concurrently by subsequent connections, potentially resulting in data being returned to the wrong user and other errors.

Name: Apache Tomcat HTTP/2 Protocol DoS Vulnerability (MadeYouReset) - Linux
description: Apache Tomcat is prone to is prone to a denial of service (DoS) vulnerability in the HTTP/2 protocol dubbed 'MadeYouReset'.
detection_result: Solution: Solution type: VendorFix Update to version 9.0.108, 10.1.44, 11.0.10 or later.
detection_method: Checks if a vulnerable version is present on the target host.
Details: Apache Tomcat HTTP/2 Protocol DoS Vulnerability (MadeYouReset) - Linux OID:1.3.6.1.4.1.25623.1.0.171672 Version used: 2025-08-26T05:39:52Z
impact: A mismatch caused by client-triggered server-sent stream resets between HTTP/2 specifications and the internal architectures of some HTTP/2 implementations may result in excessive server resource consumption leading to denial-of-service (DoS). By opening streams and then rapidly triggering the server to reset them, using malformed frames or flow control errors, an attacker can exploit incorrect stream accounting allowing unbounded concurrent streams on a single connection.
solution: Vendor fix: Update to version 9.0.108, 10.1.44, 11.0.10 or later.
insight: A mismatch caused by client-triggered server-sent stream resets between HTTP/2 specifications and the internal architectures of some HTTP/2 implementations may result in excessive server resource consumption leading to denial-of-service (DoS). Streams reset by the server are considered closed at the protocol level, even though backend processing continues, allowing a client to cause the server to handle an unbounded number of concurrent streams on a single connection.

Name: Apache Tomcat Information Disclosure Vulnerability (Mar 2023) - Linux
description: Apache Tomcat is prone to an information disclosure vulnerability.
detection_method: Checks if a vulnerable version is present on the target host. Details: Apache Tomcat Information Disclosure Vulnerability (Mar 2023) - Linux OID:1.3.6.1.4.1.25623.1.0.104653 Version used: 2024-06-07T05:05:42Z
impact: Session cookies created by Tomcat did not include the secure attribute when RemoteIpFilter is used with X-Forwarded-Proto set to https, which could result in the user agent transmitting the session cookie over an insecure channel.
insight: When using the RemoteIpFilter with requests received from a reverse proxy via HTTP that include the X-Forwarded-Proto header set to https, session cookies created by Tomcat did not include the secure attribute. This could result in the user agent transmitting the session cookie over an insecure channel.

detection_result: The following response / ICMP packet has been received:
detection_method: Sends an ICMP Timestamp (Type 13) request and checks if a Timestamp Reply (Type 14) is received.
Details: ICMP Timestamp Reply Information Disclosure OID:1.3.6.1.4.1.25623.1.0.103190
Version used: 2025-01-21T05:37:33Z
impact: This information could theoretically be used to exploit weak time-based random number generators in other services.
solution: Disable the support for ICMP timestamp on the remote host completely
Protect the remote host by a rewall, and block ICMP packets passing through the rewall in either direction (either completely or only for untrusted networks)
insight: The Timestamp Reply is an ICMP message which replies to a Timestamp message. It consists of the originating timestamp sent by the sender of the Timestamp as well as a receive timestamp and a transmit timestamp.

description: Apache Tomcat is prone to an information disclosure vulnerability.

insight: The simplied implementation of blocking reads and writes introduced in Tomcat 10 and back- ported to Tomcat 9.0.47 onwards exposed a long standing (but extremely hard to trigger) concurrency bug that could cause client connections to share an Http11Processor instance resulting in responses, or part responses, to be received by the wrong client.
